biological.citation: Myeloperoxidase-anchored ENO1 mediates neutrophil extracellular trap DNA to enhance Treg differentiation via IFITM2 during sepsis (PMID: 40892462)
biological.summary: RAP1B is activated downstream of IFITM2 (a DNA receptor on NET-exposed CD4+ T cells) and activates ERK signaling to promote Treg differentiation during sepsis-induced immunosuppression. The IFITM2-RAP1B-ERK axis is a key molecular mechanism regulating Treg differentiation in response to neutrophil extracellular traps.
biological.significance: ENO1 inhibition significantly attenuated NET-induced Treg differentiation and alleviated sepsis in mice

biological.citation: Function, Significance, and Regulation of Rap1b in Malignancy (PMID: 31679270)
biological.summary: RAP1B is a member of the RAS family of small GTPases with deregulated activation involved in multiple malignancies. RAP1B regulates cell proliferation, metastasis, angiogenesis, and treatment resistance, with overexpression in many tumors having prognostic value.

biological.citation: Somatic RAP1B gain-of-function variant underlies isolated thrombocytopenia and immunodeficiency (PMID: 39225097)
biological.summary: RAP1B acts as a molecular switch regulating cell signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell trafficking, and integrin activation in platelets and lymphocytes. Gain-of-function variants (G12E, G12V, G60R) increase RAP1B activation, talin recruitment, and integrin activation, modifying platelet activation, T cell proliferation, and migration.
biological.sample_size: 1 patient with somatic variant; comparison to germline variant patients
biological.significance: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation fully restored hemato-immunological phenotype

biological.citation: Cytoskeletal interactions of Rap1b in platelets (PMID: 8209787)
biological.summary: RAP1B (22 kDa GTP-binding protein) associates with the platelet cytoskeleton in thrombin-activated platelets with biphasic kinetics. RAP1B may promote assembly of multi-protein complexes at the plasma membrane during platelet cell activation, similar to its homolog BUD1 in yeast.

RAP1B, a Ras family member, is regulated by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway alongside Rho family GTPases. This ubiquitin-mediated regulation of RAP1B plays important roles in controlling cell polarity, migration, cell transformation, and actin dynamics.

biological.citation: Hepatocyte-specific RAP1B deficiency ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity and liver inflammation in mice (PMID: 40083059)
biological.summary: RAP1B regulates hepatic lipid metabolism and inflammation. Liver-specific RAP1B knockout mice showed reduced body weight, hepatic lipid accumulation, and decreased MAPK(p38) and NF-κB signaling, while RAP1B overexpression increased lipogenesis and inflammation.
biological.sample_size: Liver-specific knockout and overexpression mouse models; AML12 hepatocyte cell line
biological.significance: Significant reductions in body weight, fat pad size, liver mass, and hepatic lipid accumulation in LKO mice

biological.citation: Host Cell Rap1b mediates cAMP-dependent invasion by Trypanosoma cruzi (PMID: 36897926)
biological.summary: RAP1B is activated downstream of the cAMP/Epac pathway and mediates Trypanosoma cruzi invasion of host cells. RAP1B relocalizes to the parasite entry site, and PKA-dependent phosphorylation of RAP1B antagonizes the pathway. MEK/ERK signaling acts downstream of cAMP/Epac/RAP1B-mediated invasion.
biological.sample_size: Multiple cell lines; pull-down experiments with Rap1b-GTP
biological.significance: Constitutively active Rap1b-G12V mutant strongly suggests RAP1B participation in invasion pathway

biological.citation: Targeting Rap1b signaling cascades with CDNF: Mitigating platelet activation, plasma oxylipins and reperfusion injury in stroke (PMID: 39256999)
biological.summary: RAP1B activation regulates the Rap1b-MAPK-PLA2 signaling pathway in platelets, controlling thromboxane A2 release and platelet-induced inflammation. CDNF antagonizes RAP1B activation by interfering with GTP binding, reducing platelet aggregation and neuroinflammation in stroke models.
biological.sample_size: Rat ischemic stroke model; platelets from hemorrhagic stroke patients; BV2 microglial cells
biological.significance: CDNF administration significantly reduces platelet activation, infarct volume, and neurological deficits in stroke model

biological.citation: Cholesterol neutralized vemurafenib treatment by promoting melanoma stem-like cells via its metabolite 27-hydroxycholesterol (PMID: 38775844)
biological.summary: RAP1B expression is upregulated by the cholesterol metabolite 27-hydroxycholesterol (27HC), which activates Rap1-PI3K/AKT signaling to promote melanoma cell growth and vemurafenib resistance. 27HC increases both RAP1A and RAP1B expression and enhances AKT phosphorylation.
biological.sample_size: Melanoma cell lines and patient samples
biological.significance: CYP27A1 inhibition attenuates cholesterol-induced melanoma growth and abrogates vemurafenib resistance
